g: Ustedes imperative and como + role
‘Imiten’ directly commands the plural audience. ‘Como hijos muy amados’ states the identity or role from which the imitation proceeds.
e: como hijos muy amados
Como means ‘as’ here, not merely ‘like.’ Muy intensifies amados, which agrees with masculine plural hijos.

g: Así como introduces the model
‘Así como Cristo nos amó y se entregó’ means ‘just as Christ loved us and gave himself.’ Two coordinated preterites define the comparison.
e: ofrenda y sacrificio fragante para Dios
Ofrenda and sacrificio are coordinated sacrificial terms; fragante agrees directly with singular sacrificio and describes it as a pleasing offering.

g: Ni siquiera + passive infinitive
‘Ni siquiera debe mencionarse’ means ‘must not even be mentioned.’ Se makes mencionar passive, with the listed conduct as grammatical subject.
e: no es propio del pueblo santo de Dios
Ser propio de means ‘to be fitting or characteristic of.’ Del contracts de + el before pueblo.

g: Tampoco ...; haya más bien ...
Tampoco extends the prohibition; haya is present subjunctive used as an exhortation, and más bien introduces the preferred alternative.
e: todo lo cual está fuera de lugar
Todo lo cual refers back to the entire preceding list. Estar fuera de lugar is the idiom ‘to be inappropriate’ or ‘out of place.’

g: Nadie que + present subjunctive
‘Nadie que sea ... tendrá’ uses subjunctive sea because the negative antecedent nadie denies the existence of any qualifying person.
e: es decir, idólatra
Es decir introduces a clarification: in this sentence the avaro is characterized as an idólatra, linking greed with misplaced worship.

g: Que nadie + subjunctive prohibition
‘Que nadie los engañe’ uses present subjunctive as an indirect command: ‘Let no one deceive you.’ Los is the direct object.
e: los que viven en la desobediencia
Los que means ‘those who.’ Vivir en presents disobedience as the characteristic sphere of life of the people described.

g: No hacerse + predicate noun
‘No se hagan cómplices’ is a negative ustedes command. Hacerse + noun/adjective expresses becoming or taking on a role.
e: cómplices de ellos
Cómplice de means ‘partner with’ or ‘accomplice of.’ De ellos identifies the people whose conduct must not be shared.

g: Antes ... pero ahora ...
‘Antes eran oscuridad, pero ahora son luz’ contrasts two identities with imperfect eran and present son, rather than merely describing surroundings.
e: Vivan como hijos de luz
Vivan is an ustedes command. Como introduces the identity that should shape their conduct: ‘live as children of light.’

g: Consistir en + noun series
‘El fruto de la luz consiste en’ uses consistir en, ‘to consist of,’ before three coordinated abstract nouns.
e: toda bondad, justicia y verdad
Toda directly modifies only singular bondad but gives the three-part list a comprehensive sense: every kind of goodness, righteousness, and truth.

g: Lo que as a nominal relative
In ‘comprueben lo que agrada,’ lo que means ‘what’ or ‘that which’ and serves as the direct object of the command comprueben.
e: lo que agrada al Señor
Agradar works like gustar: the pleasing thing is the subject, and al Señor is the indirect experiencer, ‘what pleases the Lord.’

g: No ... sino más bien ...
The negative command ‘no tengan’ is followed by sino más bien to replace nonparticipation with the positive command denúncienlas.
e: nada que ver con
Tener nada que ver con, under negation, means ‘to have nothing to do with.’ Con introduces the works to be avoided.

v: it is shameful; it causes shame
g: Lo que introduces a noun clause
‘Lo que los desobedientes hacen en secreto’ is the subject matter of mencionar; lo que means ‘what’ and los desobedientes is the embedded subject.
e: aun mencionar
Aun without a written accent means ‘even’ here. It directly intensifies the infinitive mencionar: ‘even to mention.’

g: Todo lo que as subject
‘Todo lo que la luz pone al descubierto’ is the subject of se hace visible. Within it, la luz is the subject of pone.
e: se hace visible
Hacerse + adjective expresses a change of state: what light exposes ‘becomes visible,’ rather than someone actively making it visible.

v: will shine on you; give you light
g: Commands followed by a future result
The quotation coordinates tú commands despiértate and levántate, then adds future te alumbrará as their promised result.
e: levántate de entre los muertos
Levantarse de entre means ‘rise from among.’ De entre keeps the image of leaving the group described as los muertos.

g: No como ... sino como ...
‘No vivan como necios, sino como sabios’ replaces one manner of living with its opposite. Como introduces each comparison.
e: tengan cuidado de su manera de vivir
Tener cuidado de means ‘pay careful attention to.’ Su manera de vivir is the aspect the recipients must watch.

v: making the most of; taking advantage of
g: Gerund of manner
‘Aprovechando al máximo’ explains how to carry out the careful living commanded in verse 15; it is not a new finite command.
e: al máximo cada momento oportuno
Aprovechar al máximo means ‘make the most of.’ Cada takes singular momento, and oportuno marks each suitable opportunity.

g: No sean ... sino entiendan ...
Two ustedes commands form a correction: negative sean rejects foolishness, while sino introduces the positive command entiendan.
e: cuál es la voluntad del Señor
Cuál carries an accent because it introduces an indirect question after entiendan: ‘understand what the Lord's will is.’

g: Negative command contrasted with passive exhortation
‘No se emborrachen’ prohibits a process; ‘sean llenos’ uses ser + participle as a positive ustedes exhortation in the passive.
e: que lleva al desenfreno
The relative que refers to vino in this wording. Llevar a means ‘to lead to,’ and al contracts a + el before desenfreno.

g: Reciprocal se and coordinated imperatives
In ‘Anímense unos a otros,’ se has reciprocal force. Canten and alaben are additional ustedes commands joined by y.
e: con el corazón
Con el corazón describes the inward manner of singing and praising, not the musical instrument; it means ‘from the heart.’

v: in the name of; under the authority of
g: Gerund continuing the manner of Spirit-filled life
‘Dando siempre gracias’ is a gerund that adds another accompanying practice to the commands and participles of the surrounding sentence.
e: siempre gracias a Dios el Padre por todo
Dar gracias a alguien por algo is the full pattern: a marks the recipient of thanks, and por introduces the reason or occasion.

g: Pronominal command + reciprocal phrase
‘Sométanse’ is the ustedes command of someterse; unos a otros makes the reciprocal relationship explicit.
e: por reverencia a Cristo
Por gives the motivating reason, ‘out of reverence for Christ.’ Reverencia takes a before the person respected.

g: Vocative + pronominal imperative
‘Esposas’ directly addresses the group; sométanse is the ustedes command, and a sus propios esposos completes someterse a.
e: como al Señor
Como introduces comparison, ‘as to the Lord.’ Al contracts a + el and preserves the a required by someterse.

g: Así como + matching copular clauses
‘El esposo es cabeza ... así como Cristo es cabeza’ sets two ser clauses in comparison; the relative la cual refers to feminine iglesia.
e: la cual es su cuerpo
La cual is a formal feminine relative pronoun referring to la iglesia; it avoids ambiguity after the intervening title Salvador.

g: Así como ... también ...
Así como introduces the model clause, and también marks the corresponding conclusion. Deber + infinitive expresses obligation.
e: en todo
En todo means ‘in everything’ or ‘in every respect’ and gives the stated scope of the submission in this sentence.

g: Vocative command + así como comparison
‘Esposos, amen’ directly addresses husbands; así como then grounds the command in two completed actions, amó and se entregó.
e: se entregó por ella
Entregarse por alguien means ‘to give oneself up for someone.’ Ella is the feminine pronoun referring to la iglesia.

g: Purpose infinitive followed by gerund
‘Para hacerla santa’ states purpose with attached la; ‘lavándola’ then adds the means, again using la for the church.
e: mediante la palabra
Mediante means ‘through’ or ‘by means of.’ It connects the cleansing and washing language to la palabra.

g: Double pronouns in presentársela
In presentársela, se is the reflexive/indirect recipient reinforced by a sí mismo, while la is the direct object referring to la iglesia.
e: sin mancha ni arruga
Sin ... ni ... coordinates two absent defects, ‘without stain or wrinkle.’ Both nouns remain singular and without articles.

g: El que + present indicative
‘El que ama a su esposa se ama a sí mismo’ uses el que for ‘the one who’; reflexive se returns the action to that subject.
e: como a su propio cuerpo
Como introduces the comparison, while personal a appears before the human object su esposa and is echoed in the comparison.

g: Nadie ... jamás reinforces negation
‘Nadie ha odiado jamás’ combines the negative subject nadie with jamás for emphatic ‘no one has ever hated.’ No extra no is needed.
e: lo alimenta y lo cuida
The repeated direct-object pronoun lo refers to cuerpo and gives balanced verbs: one nourishes it and cares for it.

g: Porque + present indicative reason
‘Porque somos miembros’ supplies the reason for the preceding comparison. Somos is first-person plural and includes writer and readers.
e: miembros de su cuerpo
Miembros can mean organizational members or bodily limbs; paired with cuerpo, it sustains the corporate body metaphor.

g: Three coordinated future verbs
The quotation moves through dejará, se unirá, and llegarán. Singular el hombre shifts to plural los dos before llegarán.
e: los dos llegarán a ser un solo cuerpo
Llegar a ser expresses becoming. Los dos is plural, while the result after ser is the singular unity un solo cuerpo.

g: Referirse a + coordinated nouns
‘Me refiero a Cristo y a la iglesia’ uses referirse a; the preposition a is repeated before each coordinated referent.
e: Esto es un misterio profundo
Esto is a neuter demonstrative summarizing the preceding union language; profundo evaluates that whole matter, not a masculine noun nearby.

g: Third-person exhortations
‘Cada uno ... ame’ and ‘que la esposa respete’ use present subjunctive as exhortations directed to each spouse.
e: como a sí mismo
Sí is the stressed reflexive pronoun after a preposition and carries an accent; mismo reinforces that the reference returns to cada uno.
